prerequisites: Modul "Grundlagen der Elektrotechnik" (especially complex AC calculations)

learning_outcomes.text: Students build broad and integrated knowledge and understanding of the generation, transmission, distribution, and utilization of electrical energy, especially in public supply networks. They possess basic knowledge of protection concepts in public and private electrical networks and the associated protection technology.
Building on the course "Electrical Energy Systems", they have deepened their basic knowledge regarding the understanding of the structure and function of electrical networks.

Students know the structure of electrical networks at all voltage levels and the usual structuring into network components, as well as the fundamental procedures for calculating the network situation in normal operation and in case of faults. They have independently applied computer-aided procedures and methods to analyze and design electrical networks.

Students who have successfully completed this module are able to apply fundamental job-related knowledge, procedures, skills, and techniques to independently carry out standard tasks in electrical network planning.

Students can structure the knowledge gained in experimental work in various professional forms (protocols, spreadsheets with graphical result representation) and explain the results in individual discussions and as a group, and defend them in critical discussion with third parties.

Students understand the importance of electrical networks as a prerequisite for supplying society with electrical energy and the importance of careful planning of this long-lasting and costly infrastructure. They have developed an understanding that proposed technical solution alternatives require justification to various external interest groups, and in particular, that customers on the public supply network must be granted non-discriminatory access. For an understanding of the natural monopoly character of networks and the market opportunities in generation, trading, and sales, reference is made to the module "Liberalization and Regulation in the Energy Industry".

syllabus_topics: Structure and behavior of operating equipment
assessment_rules: The graded examination is either an oral examination with randomly selected questions from the entire course content (including lab experiments) or a 2-hour written exam. The ungraded assessment involves a maximum of five small experimental works in the laboratory practical. Each experiment must be prepared independently, carried out under instructor supervision, and may require a written or oral evaluation depending on the instructions.
